jobs.title: Lead Financial Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Req ID: 18482

Description:

**Aramco energizes the world economy.**

Aramco occupies a special position in the global energy industry. We are one of the world’s largest producers of hydrocarbon energy and chemicals, with among the lowest Upstream carbon intensities of any major producer.

With our significant investment in technology and infrastructure, we strive to maximize the value of the energy we produce for the world along with a commitment to enhance Aramco’s value to society.

Headquartered in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and with offices around the world, we combine market discipline with a generations’ spanning view of the future, born of our nine decades experience as responsible stewards of the Kingdom’s vast hydrocarbon resources. This responsibility has driven us to deliver significant societal and economic benefits to not just the Kingdom, but also to a vast number of communities, economies, and countries that rely on the vital and reliable energy that we supply.

We are one of the most profitable companies in the world, as well as amongst the top five global companies by market capitalization.

**Overview**
------------

We are seeking an Mergers and Acquisitions Analyst (M&A) to join the M&A Advisory Department, which is part of the Finance organization. The M&A Advisory Department provides finance input to transactions throughout the transaction process, including structuring, valuation, due diligence, and support to negotiations and documentation, as well as providing objective and independent advice to executive management relating to transactions.

Your primary role is to supports the development and execution of large and complex international transactions by acting as a single point of contact for all finance-related inputs throughout the lifecycle of transactions, often against challenging deadlines. Activities including screening opportunities, developing optimal deal structuring and framing options, formulating valuation and bid price recommendations, conducting financial due diligence, advising on accounting aspects of transactions, reviewing and providing advisory on definitive agreements, purchase price adjustments, integration planning, and post-transaction evaluations. The M&A Finance Lead will interface with other transaction team members and specialists within Finance such as Treasury, Controller’s and Embedded Finance, and other corporate organization. The M&A Finance Lead is also required to present an objective and independent assessment of transactions to executive management to support decision-making. The position holder is expected to develop, coach, and mentor staff as a core part of the role.

**Duties and Responsibilities**
-------------------------------

As a successful candidate you will be preforming the following;

* Represent Finance as a core member in a multi-functional transaction execution team, providing end-to-end finance support to transactions.
* As Finance transaction lead, presents expert and objective assessment of transaction to the Executive Management to support decision-making in all aspects of transactions, including strategic assessment, partner selection, economic viability, deal structuring options, closing mechanisms, integration planning and accounting and financial implication.
* Assess deal structuring and commercial options. Screens and evaluates transaction counterparties and joint venture partners. responsible for the valuation and economic assessment of the opportunity, including EV to Equity adjustments, ensuring that financial models and outputs are prepared according to Aramco standards, that risks are considered, and that input assumptions are robust and documented, and that deficiencies and risks are considered.
* Manages external Financial and Accounting Advisors on transactions. Develops relationships to bring external perspectives on the M&A landscape to the Company.
* Prepares bid price recommendation proposal for senior management reflecting project specific competitive landscape, economic and industry considerations.
* Manages the financial due diligence process (lead the activities of advisors), ensuring that due diligence findings are communicated to executive management and factored into valuation and/or definitive agreements.
* Interface with finance and other functions (Treasury, Controllers, Embedded Finance, Strategy & Market Analysis and Law) to seek subject matter expert advice in delivering the requirements of transactions.
* Coordinate solutions with external advisors and internal stakeholders on the accounting aspects of transactions.
* Contributes to definitive agreements and is responsible for purchase price adjustments and post-transaction purchase price allocation.
* Is a member of the integration planning team, advising on finance aspects of integration.
* Develops, coaches and mentors team members on transactions.
* Contributes to the continuous improvement of processes and methodologies to become a center of excellence of M&A execution for the Company.
* Provides ad hoc financial analysis activities including on transfer pricing, impairment reviews, government incentives, and group policy reviews.

**Minimum Requirements**
------------------------

* You will hold a Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Management, or Engineering.Possession of an advanced business degree (e.g. MBA) or Accounting qualification, CPA, CA, CFA is preferred.
* 15+ years relevant experience in conducting M&A transactions, including expertise in financial analysis likely gained in leading investment banks, accounting firms, or large international corporations.
* Significant experience in large and complex cross-border transactions preferably in energy or natural resources sectors.
* Prior experience in LNG transactions and deep knowledge of the segment is highly preferred.
* Expert level knowledge and use of financial analysis tools and methodologies, understanding of financial statements

jobs.title: Portfolio Manager, Centre of Revenue Intelligence, MEA APAC
jobs.description:
**Company Description**

Accor is a world leader in the hotel industry, present in 110 countries, with more than 5,500 hotels and 10,000 restaurants and bars. The group deploys an integrated hotel ecosystem that is among the most diversified in the sector, notably associating luxury and high-end brands, mid-range and economic offers, exclusive lifestyle concepts, venues for shows and entertainment, clubs, restaurants and bars, private residences, shared accommodation, Qantas Lounges, concierge services and co-working spaces. Accor has a portfolio of incomparable brands, led by more than 300,000 employees around the world.

 **Job Description**

We are seeking a commercially driven Portfolio Manager to lead the revenue performance of an assigned portfolio of hotels across the MEA APAC region. In this role, you will develop and execute revenue management strategies that maximise RevPAR, market share and profitability, while partnering closely with each hotel's leadership team to achieve their commercial objectives.

Reporting to the Senior Portfolio Manager, Centre of Revenue Intelligence, you will act as the trusted commercial advisor to General Managers and Executive Committees, balancing strategic planning with day to day revenue optimisation. Working remotely across multiple hotels, you will leverage market intelligence, data-driven insights and strong stakeholder relationships to influence commercial decisions and deliver measurable business outcomes.

**Getting to know the role and your responsibilities**

* Develop and execute pricing, inventory and distribution strategies aligned with brand standards and regional commercial objectives.
* Manage forecasting, segmentation, pricing and inventory planning to optimise revenue performance.
* Build strong partnerships with General Managers, Executive Committees and key commercial stakeholders, including Directors of Sales & Marketing, Directors of Sales and Finance leaders.
* Analyse market trends, competitor activity, demand patterns and business performance to identify revenue opportunities and inform commercial strategy.
* Drive agreed commercial initiatives to improve RevPAR, increase market share and optimise the cost of sale.
* Lead daily revenue briefings and facilitate weekly and monthly RevMAX meetings in line with the assigned service tier.
* Conduct post event and post period analysis to evaluate commercial performance and identify continuous improvement opportunities.
* Monitor the effectiveness of agreed revenue initiatives, providing regular updates and recommendations to hotel leadership.
* Champion best-practice revenue management across the portfolio, supporting hotels to maximise commercial performance through strategic guidance and data-driven decision-making.

  
**Qualifications**  

* Bachelor's degree in Hospitality, Business, Commerce or a related discipline.
* 3–5 years' experience in Revenue Management, ideally supporting multiple hotels or a regional portfolio.
* Strong expertise in revenue management principles, pricing strategies and distribution channels, with advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Business Intelligence (BI) tools and IDeaS RMS.
* Commercially astute, with strong analytical and problem-solving skills and the ability to translate data into actionable business strategies.
* Confident communicator with the ability to influence and build credibility with senior stakeholders, including General Managers and Executive Committees.
* Highly organised, proactive and able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, remote environment.
* Demonstrated accountability, resilience and a strong customer-focused mindset, with a genuine commitment to delivering commercial results.
* Fluency in English and at least one additional language, written and spoken, is required. Two additional languages are preferred.

  
**Additional Information**  

* Enjoy discounted Heartist® rates across Accor's global network of hotels, food and beverage venues, and wellness centres.
* Explore international career opportunities across Accor's hotel portfolio.
* Benefit from continuous learning and professional development, including Accor's Revenue Management Academy certification.

This role is based in Dubai, United Arab Emirates.

Candidate screening and interviews may be conducted prior to the closing date of the advertisement. Accor reserves the right to close applications for the position prior to the advertised date. We encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible.
